## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
set.seed(123)
library(grf)
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
# read in the data
observational_df <- read.csv("/nsw_observational_resampling_trimmed_new.csv")
experimental_df <- read.csv("/nsw_experimental.csv")
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
# rowbind the data
experimental_df$S <- 1
observational_df$S <- 0

data_all <- rbind(experimental_df, observational_df)
```

```{r}
features <- c("age","educ","black","hisp","marr","nodegree","re74","re75")

Y <- data_all$re78
A <- data_all$treat

X <- data_all[, features]
S <- data_all$S

n <- nrow(data_all)
K <- 5
```

```{r}
# k fold indicator
use_k_fold <- TRUE
```

```{r}
# propensity score
if (use_k_fold == FALSE){
  prop_model <- glm(
    A ~ .,
    data = data.frame(A = A, X),
    family = binomial()
  )
  
  e_hat <- predict(
    prop_model,
    newdata = X,
    type = "response"
  )
}
```

```{r}
if (use_k_fold == TRUE){
  n <- nrow(data_all)
  K <- 5
  
  fold_id <- sample(rep(1:K, length.out = n))
  
  e_hat <- rep(NA, n)

  features <- c("age","educ","black","hisp","marr","nodegree","re74","re75")
  
  for (k in 1:K) {
  
    train_idx <- which(fold_id != k)
    test_idx  <- which(fold_id == k)
  
    train_data <- data.frame(A = A[train_idx], X[train_idx, ])
    test_data  <- X[test_idx, ]
  
    # fit model on training fold
    prop_model_k <- glm(
      A ~ .,
      data = train_data,
      family = binomial()
    )
  
    # predict on held-out fold
    e_hat[test_idx] <- predict(
      prop_model_k,
      newdata = test_data,
      type = "response"
    )
  }
}
```

```{r}
# outcome model
if (use_k_fold == FALSE) {
  mu_model <- lm(re78 ~ ., data = data.frame(re78 = Y, X))
  mu_hat <- predict(mu_model, newdata = X)
}
```

```{r}
if (use_k_fold == TRUE){
  n <- nrow(data_all)
  K <- 5
  
  mu_hat <- rep(NA, n)
  
  # fold_id <- sample(rep(1:K, length.out = n))
  
  for (k in 1:K) {
  
    train_idx <- which(fold_id != k)
    test_idx  <- which(fold_id == k)
  
    fit <- lm(re78 ~ ., data = data.frame(re78 = Y[train_idx], X[train_idx, ]))
  
    mu_hat[test_idx] <- predict(fit, newdata = X[test_idx, ])
  }
}
```

```{r}
# used Claude to help generate code
# r loss minimization
# residuals
Y_tilde <- Y - mu_hat
A_tilde <- A - e_hat

# pseudo-outcome and weights
W <- Y_tilde / A_tilde
weights <- A_tilde^2

# weighted regression to estimate tau(X)
tau_model <- lm(W ~ ., data    = data.frame(W = W, X), weights = weights)
tau_hat <- predict(tau_model, newdata = X)

# summary
summary(tau_hat)
mean(tau_hat)  # average treatment effect estimate
```

```{r}
summary(tau_model)
```

Mean(\\hat{\\tau}) = -131.78 is the average treatment effect across individuals in our dataset. The difference in income between the treatment and control groups is \$-131.78, so the training program decreased earnings, on average.

```{r}
hist(tau_hat, xlab = "tau hat", main = "Estimated Treatment Effect Across Individuals", breaks = 50)
```

For many individuals, it seems the treatment (training program) did not have much of an effect on their income, as the tau hat value for many individuals falls around 0.
